messages:
Ada: FYI I spun up a long-session replay and saw steady memory creep + rising page_reads over ~3h. kv.fragmentation_ratio goes from ~0.12 -> 0.28, hit_rate nominal. attaching quick prometheus queries and a tiny profile dump.

Ada: PromQL I used:
```
# per-shard read amplification (reads per logical request)
sum(rate(kv_page_reads_total[5m])) by (shard) / sum(rate(kv_requests_total[5m])) by (shard)

# fragmentation ratio (est)
avg(kv_fragmented_bytes_total / kv_allocated_bytes_total) by (instance)
```

Matt: +1 seeing similar in canary yesterday. did you correlate with long-context (>8k) sessions or just overall?

Ada: mostly long-context. I filtered by label `session_length_bucket="8k+"` and the per-request read amplification spikes.

Sree: Two quick asks: (1) can we add an `eviction_reason` label to `kv_eviction_total` (age/load/compact) so we can split mechanical compactions vs reactive evictions? (2) add `kv_compaction_count` so we can see when compaction runs correlate with fragmentation drops.

Ada: yep can add labels. I sketched a lightweight counter patch: `kv_compaction_events_total{shard, compact_type}`.

Luis: Also consider a small gauge `kv_cache_freeze_active` when we temporarily pin pages for long-generation requests — freeze periods seem to increase reuse but also block compaction. If freeze windows are long they explain memory growth.

Jen: For the dashboard layout, proposal: Top row: read_amplification (per-shard heatmap), global hit_rate sparkline, residency_p50/p95. Middle: fragmentation_ratio (trend), compaction_events (bars), eviction_by_reason (stacked). Bottom: sample traces with a link to the profile S3 object. Alert: read_amplification > 5 for 10m on any shard -> P2.

Ada: sample trace link: s3://redwood-profiles/2256789012/kv-longsession-2026-03-15.pb.gz

Matt: Can we get promql for the read_amplification heatmap? might want to do `increase(kv_page_reads_total[15m]) / increase(kv_requests_total[15m])` then use `by (shard)` and map to heatmap.

Ada: yeah here's the exact one I used: `((increase(kv_page_reads_total[15m]) / ignoring(instance) group_left() increase(kv_requests_total[15m])))` — Grafana accepts it if you set the time window to 15m.

Sree: Note about sampling bias: our current sampler only captures 1% of sessions and preferentially samples short sessions in the aggregator. We should make the sampler stratified by `session_length_bucket` and `model_family`. Otherwise long-context edge behaviors are underrepresented.

Luis: ops note: if we increase sampler for long sessions, watch cardinality on labels (shard, model, customer_tier). recommend downsampling before shipping to prometheus remote_write.

Ada: quick log excerpt from node-7 at 03:14 UTC (truncated):
```
[03:14:05] shard=7 session_id=abc123 pages_read=412 reads_per_req=6.8 frag_ratio=0.27 compaction=0
[03:14:20] shard=7 session_id=abc123 pages_read=417 reads_per_req=7.1 frag_ratio=0.28 compaction=0
```

Jen: +1 on stratified sampler. For alerts I'd rather P3 for now but with a runbook: if read_amplification > 8 for >30m escalate to runtime oncall.

Matt: action items: Ada will add `kv_compaction_events_total` and `eviction_reason` label by EOD Thu. Sree will flip sampler to stratified experiment and report sample counts. Jen will draft Grafana panels and alert thresholds. Luis will add `kv_cache_freeze_active` gauge.

Ada: I'll open PRs and link them here. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/483 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/210

ops-bot: deploy pipeline started for telemetry changes (pipeline #5213) :gear:

Matt: thanks — once the metrics land we can iterate on thresholds. also we should add a small synthetic test that runs long-context replay nightly and pushes to test cluster so dashboards have signal.

Ada: good call, adding synthetic job to cron-runbook.

Sree: note for later: we might need a compaction budget per-shard to avoid compaction storms causing tail latency spikes.

Luis: :eyes: noted.

Jen: I'll sketch the panel JSON and paste in the PR.

Ada: thx all.

Jen: next meetup to review dashboards Wed 10am.

Ada: ack :thumbsup:
